title: The English Alphabet & Letter Names vs Sounds
objectives: Name the 26 letters of the English alphabet
Distinguish letter names from letter sounds

teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: The English Alphabet & Letter Names vs Sounds. Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner tries to read 'cat' using letter names (/siː-eɪ-tiː/).
💡 Solution: Demonstrate blending letter sounds /k/-/æ/-/t/.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: The English Alphabet & Letter Names vs Sounds
1. Definition: The English alphabet consists of 26 letters (5 vowels: A, E, I, O, U and 21 consonants).
2. Rule: Letter names (A = /eɪ/) differ from letter sounds (A = /æ/ in cat). Consonants are mostly consistent.
3. Why? English spelling is historical, so letter names help in spelling aloud while letter sounds help in reading.
4. How to recognize? Observe single letters in isolation vs in CVC words.
5. Common examples: A /eɪ/ (name) vs /æ/ (apple), B /biː/ (bat), C /siː/ (cat), D /diː/ (dog), E /iː/ (egg)
6. Counter-examples: Vowel digraphs like EA where two letters make one sound.
7. Exceptions: Y acts as a consonant at start (/j/ in yes) and vowel at end (/iː/ in happy).
8. Common mistakes: Confusing letter names with letter sounds when reading words.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Letter NAME is how you spell it; letter SOUND is how you read it!
10. Key vocabulary: alphabet, vowel, consonant, letter name, letter sound, spell
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟢 A1
13. Associated Visual: 🔤 Grid of 26 letters with names and primary sounds.
14. Key Takeaway: 26 letters, 44 sounds! Learn the sound of each letter for reading.

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: How many letters are in the English alphabet? (26 letters)
CCQ 2: Is the letter name of 'A' (/eI/) the same as its sound in 'cat' (/æ/)? (No, name is /eI/, sound is /æ/)
CCQ 3: When is Y a consonant? (At the start of a word, like 'yes')

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Spell these words using letter names, then pronounce using letter sounds:
🎯 Item: cat ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: C-A-T -> /kæt/
🎯 Item: dog ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: D-O-G -> /dɒg/
🎯 Item: pen ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: P-E-N -> /pɛn/
